arxiv-2303-00652.title: Finding the right XAI method — A Guide for the Evaluation and Ranking of Explainable AI Methods in Climate Science
arxiv-2303-00652.creator: Philine Bommer, Marlene Kretschmer, Anna Hedström, Dilyara Bareeva, Marina M.-C. Höhne
arxiv-2303-00652.description: Abstract Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods shed light on the predictions of machine learning algorithms. Several different approaches exist and have already been applied in climate science. However, usually missing ground truth explanations complicate their evaluation and comparison, subsequently impeding the choice of the XAI method.

arxiv-2307-03864.title: When Do Transformers Shine in RL? Decoupling Memory from Credit Assignment
arxiv-2307-03864.creator: Tianwei Ni, Michel Ma, Benjamin Eysenbach, Pierre-Luc Bacon
arxiv-2307-03864.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms face two distinct challenges: learning effective representations of past and present observations, and determining how actions influence future returns. Both challenges involve modeling long-term dependencies. The Transformer architecture has been very successful to solve problems that involve long-term dependencies, including in the RL domain.

arxiv-2408-01772.title: Investment strategies based on forecasts are (almost) useless
arxiv-2408-01772.creator: Michael Weba
arxiv-2408-01772.description: Abstract Abstract . Several studies on portfolio construction reveal that sensible strategies essentially yield the same results as their nonsensical inverted counterparts; moreover, random portfolios managed by Malkiel’s dart-throwing monkey would outperform the cap-weighted benchmark index. Forecasting the future development of stock returns is an important aspect of portfolio assessment.

arxiv-2409-03999.title: The LBT Satellites of Nearby Galaxies Survey (LBT-SONG): The Diffuse Satellite Population of Local Volume Hosts
arxiv-2409-03999.creator: A. Bianca Davis 1,2, Christopher T. Garling 2,3,4, Anna M. Nierenberg 5, Annika H. G. Peter 1,2,3,6, Amy Sardone 2,3,8, Christopher S. Kochanek 2,3, Adam K. Leroy 2,3, Kirsten J. Casey 1,2, Richard W. Pogge 2,3, Daniella M. Roberts 1,2, David J. Sand 7, Johnny P. Greco 1,2,8
arxiv-2409-03999.description: Abstract We present the results of the Large Binocular Telescope Satellites Of Nearby Galaxies Survey (LBT-SONG) “Far Sample,” including survey completeness estimates. We find 10 satellite candidates in the inner virial regions of 13 star-forming galaxies outside the Local Group.

arxiv-2410-02110.title: Can LLMs Reliably Simulate Human Learner Actions? A Simulation Authoring Framework for Open-Ended Learning Environments
arxiv-2410-02110.creator: Amogh Mannekote, Adam Davies, Jina Kang, Kristy Elizabeth Boyer
arxiv-2410-02110.description: Abstract Simulating learner actions helps stress-test open-ended interactive learning environments and prototype new adaptations before deployment. While recent studies show the promise of using large language models (LLMs) for simulating human behavior, such approaches have not gone beyond rudimentary proof-of-concept stages due to key limitations.

arxiv-2506-00880.title: ModuLM: Enabling Modular and Multimodal Molecular Relational Learning with Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-00880.creator: Zhuo Chen, Yizhen Zheng, Huan Yee Koh, Hongxin Xiang, Linjiang Chen, Wenjie Du, Yang Wang
arxiv-2506-00880.description: Abstract Molecular Relational Learning (MRL) aims to understand interactions between molecular pairs, playing a critical role in advancing biochemical research. With the recent development of large language models (LLMs), a growing number of studies have explored the integration of MRL with LLMs and achieved promising results.

arxiv-2510-04841.title: One-Loop Effects in the Neutrino Matter Potential and Implications for Non-Standard Interactions
arxiv-2510-04841.description: Abstract In this work, we emphasize that it is necessary to take into account one-loop corrections of 2.0 % 2.0\% to the neutrino matter potential in the precision measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters and in the experimental searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model.

pmc-10674459.title: Designing a Compact Dual-Band, Dual-Polarized Antenna for Biotelemetry Communications Using the Characteristic Mode Method
pmc-10674459.creator: Xiaoming Xu, Zhiwei Song, Yuchao Wang, Ahmed Jamal Abdullah Al-Gburi
pmc-10674459.description: A compact dual-band, dual-polarized, implantable antenna was designed using the characteristic mode method for operation in the wireless medical telemetry service (WMTS) band (1.4 GHz) and the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band (2.45 GHz). By utilizing slotting techniques and materials with high dielectric constants, the antenna volume was minimized to 47.

pmc-10710559.title: Association of an inter‐arm systolic blood pressure difference with all‐cause and cardiovascular mortality: A meta‐analysis of cohort studies
pmc-10710559.creator: Min Li, Fangfang Fan, Lin Qiu, Wei Ma, Yan Zhang
pmc-10710559.description: This meta‐analysis evaluated the potential association of a simultaneously measured inter‐arm systolic blood pressure difference (IASBPD) and all‐cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality. The Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, and PubMed databases were searched through to April 14, 2023 for relevant literature. The outcomes were the associations of IASBPD with all‐cause and cardiovascular mortality.

pmc-11356365.title: Feasibility of Early Surgical Treatment for Adolescent Patients with Prolactinoma: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-11356365.creator: Yu-Hung Tsai, Chi-Ruei Li, Yu-Ting Wang, Se-Yi Chen
pmc-11356365.description: Background and Objectives: Prolactinomas are the most common pituitary adenomas, comprising 30–50% of such tumors. These adenomas cause hyperprolactinemia, leading to decreased fertility, reduced energy and libido, and galactorrhea. Diagnosing and treating prolactinomas in adolescents present unique challenges, as symptoms may be confused with age-related developmental variations.

pmc-11478993.title: Synthesis and Redox Activity of Polyenaminones for Sustainable Energy Storage Applications
pmc-11478993.creator: Tomaž Kotnik, Svit Menart, Žan Adam, Jan Bitenc, Luka Ciber, Uroš Grošelj, Nejc Petek, Bogdan Štefane, Jurij Svete, Boštjan Genorio, Sheng-Heng Chung
pmc-11478993.description: In the search for novel polymeric molecules that could be used as electroactive materials, seven novel polyenaminones were prepared in high yields by the transaminative polymerization of resorcinol-derived bis-enaminones with m- and p-phenylenediamine and with 2,5-diaminohydroquinone. The obtained polymers show very low solubility in organic solvents and absorb UV light and visible light at wavelengths below 500 nm.

pmc-11535711.title: Multicenter validation of an RNA-based assay to predict anti-PD-1 disease control in patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: the PREDAPT study
pmc-11535711.creator: Kevin C Flanagan, Jon Earls, Jeffrey Hiken, Rachel L Wellinghoff, Michelle M Ponder, Howard L McLeod, William H Westra, Vera Vavinskaya, Leisa Sutton, Ida Deichaite, Orlan K Macdonald, Karim Welaya, James Wade III, Georges Azzi, Andrew W Pippas, Jennifer Slim, Bruce Bank, Xingwei Sui, Steven E Kossm
pmc-11535711.description: BackgroundDespite advances in cancer care and detection, >65% of patients with squamous cell cancer of the head and neck (HNSCC) will develop recurrent and/or metastatic disease. The prognosis for these patients is poor with a 5-year overall survival of 39%.

pmc-11678616.title: The Role of Transcranial Ultrasound Imaging in Intensive Care Treatment of Decompressive Hemicraniectomy Patients: A Retrospective Single-Center Analysis
pmc-11678616.creator: Martin Petkov, Ralf Becker, Max Schneider, Michal Hlavac, Andreas Knoll, Christian Rainer Wirtz, Ralph König, Andrej Pala
pmc-11678616.description: Background: Post-hemicraniectomy patients often need extended intensive care treatment. While computed tomography (CT) is considered the gold standard for regular imaging, its frequent use could be linked to adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to assess bedside transcranial ultrasound (TUS) to capture intracranial anatomical structures and pathologies.

pmc-12645215.title: Immunopeptidomics Workflow for Isolation and LC-MS/MS Analysis of MHC Class I-Bound Peptides Under Hypoxic Conditions
pmc-12645215.creator: Hala Estephan, Ester M Hammond, Eleni Adamopoulou
pmc-12645215.description: Immunopeptidomics enables the identification of peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, offering insights into antigen presentation and immune recognition. Understanding these mechanisms in hypoxic conditions is crucial for deciphering immune responses within the tumor microenvironment. Current immunopeptidomics approaches do not capture hypoxia-induced changes in the repertoire of MHC-presented peptides.
